text: Theo schedules one combined game-day drill instead of five separate tests, because the sale-window ceiling, the spread constraint, the PodDisruptionBudget, and the audit fixes are meant to work together under real load — the exact condition nobody fully tested before the original incident.

Six drill steps, each with a pass condition decided in advance: the autoscaler reaching the new ceiling, the per-AZ panel staying in a tight band, a deliberately drained node not causing a capacity gap, the audit fixes reporting per-dimension, a real failover to the secondary cloud, and the budget alert firing correctly on the cost event.

Every step passes cleanly except one real, minor finding: the failover cutover lands a few seconds past the planned RTO, inside an acceptable margin but not instant. It's logged as a follow-up, not a failure, since it still met its own pass condition.

That finding is the more valuable outcome. A small, specific fact discovered on a controlled schedule, with time to decide whether it matters, beats discovering the same fact for the first time during a real failover under real pressure.
